extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory patent examiners (SPEs)
extracted.subtask_description: Use and selection of MPEP form paragraphs for restriction/rejoinder actions, petitions (e.g., 37 CFR 1.324), withdrawal from issue, and appeal-related communications. Specifies when to use particular form paragraphs and the procedural requirements attached to those communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoining all previously withdrawn process claims (use form paragraph 8.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] directed to an allowable product. Pursuant to the procedures set forth in MPEP § 821.04(b), claim [2], directed to the process of making or using an allowable product, previously withdrawn from consideration as a result of a restriction requirement, [3] hereby rejoined and fully examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims directed to a nonelected process invention must require all the limitations of an allowable product claim for that process invention to be rejoined (MPEP § 821.04(b)). Because all claims previously withdrawn under 37 CFR 1.142 have been rejoined, the restriction requirement is withdrawn and, once withdrawn, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable (In re Ziegler). Applicants are to be advised that continuation/divisional claims anticipated by or including all limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections. Examiner bracket-insert instructions specify claim numbers, dates, group numbers, and appropriate singular/plural forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder when LESS THAN ALL previously withdrawn claims are rejoined (use form paragraph 8.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: If LESS THAN ALL previously withdrawn process claims are being rejoined, then form paragraph 8.42 should be used instead of this form paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims directed to a nonelected process invention must require all the limitations of an allowable product claim for that process invention to be rejoined (MPEP § 821.04(b)). Use 8.42 when not all previously withdrawn claims are being rejoined; follow bracket insertion instructions for claim identification and appropriate verb forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rejoinder after first Office action if rejoined claims are unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If rejoinder occurs after the first Office action on the merits and if any of the rejoined claims are unpatentable, e.g., if a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph is made, then the next Office action may be made final if proper under MPEP § 706.07(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider finality of subsequent Office action per MPEP § 706.07(a) when rejoined claims are found unpatentable after rejoinder following the first merits action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; rejoin all previously withdrawn claims when nonelected not canceled (use 8.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. Claim [2], previously withdrawn from consideration as a result of a restriction requirement, [3] all the limitations of an allowable claim. Pursuant to the procedures set forth in MPEP § 821.04(a), the restriction requirement [4] inventions [5], as set forth in the Office action mailed on [6], is hereby withdrawn and claim [7] hereby rejoined and fully examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 8.45 whenever ALL previously withdrawn claims depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim and wherein the non-elected claims have NOT been canceled. Use other form paragraphs (8.46–8.50) as appropriate where non-elected claims have been canceled or the restriction is withdrawn only in part. Include the double patenting advisory and the 35 U.S.C. 121 inapplicability notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; nonelected claims canceled; other issues remain (use 8.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. The restriction requirement [2] inventions [4], has been [3] reconsidered in view of the allowability of claims to the elected invention pursuant to MPEP § 821.04(a). The restriction requirement is hereby withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. ... Claim [7], which required all the limitations of an allowable claim, previously withdrawn from consideration as a result of the restriction requirement, [8] canceled by applicant in the reply filed on [9]. The canceled, nonelected claim(s) may be reinstated by applicant if submitted in a timely filed amendment in reply to this action. Upon entry of the amendment, such amended claim(s) will be examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph applies where non-elected claims requiring all limitations HAVE BEEN canceled. Canceled nonelected claims can be reinstated by timely amendment in reply; upon entry they will be examined under 37 CFR 1.104. If no issues remain and application is otherwise ready for allowance, use form paragraph 8.47 or 8.47.01 instead. Include double patenting advisory and 35 U.S.C.121 notice. Bracket instructions specify wording and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; nonelected claims canceled; before final rejection; no outstanding issues (use 8.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. The restriction requirement [2] inventions [3], as set forth in the Office action mailed on [4], has been reconsidered in view of the allowability of claims to the elected invention pursuant to MPEP § 821.04(a). The restriction requirement is hereby withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. ... The canceled, nonelected claim(s) may be reinstated by applicant if submitted in an amendment, limited to the addition of such claim(s), filed within a time period of TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this letter. Upon entry of the amendment, such amended claim(s) will be examined for patentability under 37 CFR 1.104. If NO such amendment is submitted within the set time period, the application will be passed to issue. PROSECUTION ON THE MERITS IS OTHERWISE CLOSED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when there are no outstanding issues remaining and with only a PTO-90C cover sheet. Applicable when restriction requirement was between related product or process inventions and application has not been finally rejected. Includes two-month limited window for reinstatement of canceled nonelected claims by amendment limited to adding such claims; otherwise application proceeds to issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; nonelected claims canceled; after final rejection; no outstanding issues (use 8.47.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. The restriction requirement [2] inventions [3], as set forth in the Office action mailed on [4], has been reconsidered in view of the allowability of claims to the elected invention pursuant to MPEP § 821.04(a). The restriction requirement is hereby withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. Specifically, the restriction requirement of [5] is [6]. In view of the withdrawal of the restriction requirement as set forth above, applicant(s) are advised ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is applicable where a restriction requirement was made between related product inventions or related process inventions and the application has been finally rejected. Use 8.47 before final rejection. Same double patenting and 35 U.S.C.121 advisories apply. Use bracket insertion instructions as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; claims stand withdrawn as not in required form (use 8.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. The restriction requirement [2], as set forth in the Office action mailed on [3], has been reconsidered in view of the allowability of claims to the elected invention pursuant to MPEP § 821.04(a). The restriction requirement is hereby withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. Specifically, the restriction requirement of [4] is [5]. Claim [6], directed to [7] withdrawn from further consideration because [8] require all the limitations of an allowable generic linking claim as required by 37 CFR 1.141.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph applies where a restriction was made between related product or process inventions and nonelected claims are withdrawn for not being in required form per 37 CFR 1.141. Use 8.50 when some claims are no longer withdrawn. Include 35 U.S.C.121 and double patenting advisories. Bracket instructions identify which inventions and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable; some claims no longer withdrawn (use 8.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] allowable. The restriction requirement [2], as set forth in the Office action mailed on [3], has been reconsidered in view of the allowability of claims to the elected invention pursuant to MPEP § 821.04(a). The restriction requirement is hereby withdrawn as to any claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. Specifically, the restriction requirement of [4] is [5]. Claim [6], directed to [7] no longer withdrawn from consideration because the claim(s) requires all the limitations of an allowable claim. However, claim [8], directed to [9] withdrawn from consideration because [10] require all the limitations of an allowable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable where some, but not all, nonelected claims require all the limitations of an allowable claim. If all claims are in proper form, use 8.45, 8.46, or 8.47 as appropriate. Includes bracket insertion instructions and double patenting/35 U.S.C.121 advisories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory on double patenting when restriction requirement withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant(s) are advised that if any claim presented in a continuation or divisional application is anticipated by, or includes all the limitations of, a claim that is allowable in the present application, such claim may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections over the claims of the instant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This caution is repeated in many form paragraphs where the restriction requirement is withdrawn. Examiners must include this advisory to notify applicants of potential double patenting issues arising from rejoined/allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Once restriction withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 inapplicable (In re Ziegler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the restriction requirement is withdrawn, the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 are no longer applicable. See In re Ziegler, 443 F.2d 1211, 1215, 170 USPQ 129, 131-32 (CCPA 1971). See also MPEP § 804.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the reference to In re Ziegler and MPEP § 804.01 in communications when withdrawing restriction requirements and rejoining claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue because issue/publication fee not paid (37 CFR 1.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is being withdrawn from issue pursuant to 37 CFR 1.313 to permit reopening of prosecution. The reasons therefor will be communicated to you by the examiner. U.S. Patent and Trademark Office records reveal that the issue fee and the publication fee have not been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant options: if fee(s) submitted, request refund or credit to deposit account; applicant may wait until application is again found allowable or held abandoned. If allowed, previously submitted fees may be applied to a new Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due; if abandoned, applicant may request refund or credit. Examiner Note: letter is printed with USPTO letterhead and must be signed by the TC Director. Do not use this form if fees have been paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.324 (correct inventorship) granted (form paragraph 10.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a decision on the petition filed under 37 CFR 1.324. The petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to correct inventorship of an issued patent are decided by the Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE), per the Commissioner's memorandum (June 2, 1989). Prepare Certificate using form paragraph 10.15 and forward to Certificates of Correction Branch. Insert correspondence address where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandum/Certificate of Correction for inventorship (form paragraph 10.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please issue a Certificate of Correction in U.S. Letters Patent No. [4] as specified on the attached Certificate. On petition requesting issuance of a certificate for correction of inventorship pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 256, it has been found that the above identified patent improperly sets forth the inventorship. Accordingly, it is hereby certified that the correct inventorship of this patent is: [9].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal memo not to be mailed; accompany the patented file to Certificates of Correction Branch. In bracket 9, insert full name and residence (City, State) of each actual inventor. Insert SPE name and Art Unit, and sign as instructed. Two separate pages of USPTO letterhead will be printed when using this form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of a 37 CFR 1.48 request when patent already issued (treated as 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a decision on the request under 37 CFR 1.48. In view of the fact that the patent has already issued, the request under 37 CFR 1.48 has been treated as a petition to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.324. The petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward the patented file to Certificates of Correction Branch for issuance of a certificate naming only the actual inventor(s). Prepare Certificate using form paragraph 10.15. Insert correspondence address as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.324 dismissed if required items missing (pre-Sep 16, 2012 rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.324 filed before September 16, 2012, requires (1) a statement from each person who is being added as an inventor that the inventorship error occurred without any deceptive intention on their part, (2) a statement from the current named inventors who have not submitted a statement as per '(1)' either agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement, (3) a statement in compliance with 3.73(b) from all assignees of the parties submitting a statement under '(1)' and '(2)' agreeing to the change, and (4) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b). This petition lacks item(s) [7].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more items insufficient, petition should be denied (10.17) unless curable — dismissal is appropriate if cure is possible by renewed petition. Use form paragraph 10.16 only for petitions filed before September 16, 2012. Insert missing item numbers in bracket 7 and correspondence address in bracket 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.324 dismissed if required items missing (on/after Sep 16, 2012 rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.324 filed on or after September 16, 2012, requires (1) a statement from each person who is being added as an inventor and each person who is currently named as an inventor either agreeing to the change of inventorship or stating that he or she has no disagreement, (2) a statement in compliance with 37 CFR 3.73(c) from all assignees of the parties submitting a statement under '(1)' agreeing to the change, and (3) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b). This petition lacks item(s) [7].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If each of the three specified items has been submitted but one or more is insufficient, the petition should be denied (10.17) unless the deficiency can be cured by a renewed petition, in which case dismissal may be appropriate. Insert missing item numbers and correspondence address as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.324 denied — explanation requirement (form paragraph 10.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a decision on the petition filed under 37 CFR 1.324. The petition is denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 7, a full explanation of the deficiency must be provided. If the petition lacks one or more required parts set forth in 37 CFR 1.324, it should be dismissed (use form paragraph 10.14 or 10.20) rather than denied. Insert correspondence address as indicated. Forward Certificate of Correction if appropriate (instructions follow paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of requirements of 37 CFR 1.324 under 37 CFR 1.183 dismissed when statutory requirement applies (form paragraph 10.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of the rules under 37 CFR 1.183 may be granted for any requirement of the regulations which is not a requirement of the statutes. In this instance, 35 U.S.C. 256 requires [1]. Accordingly, the petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition requests waiver of requirements of 37 CFR 1.324 that are not statutory (e.g., the fee or oath/declaration by all inventors), forward to a petitions attorney in the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for decision. Use this paragraph following form paragraph 10.16 whenever waiver of statutory-required provisions is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition or request dismissed for not submitting proper fee (form paragraph 10.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s petition or request under 37 CFR [1] filed [2] is DISMISSED because the proper petition or processing fee of [3] required under 37 CFR 1.17 has not been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes enumerate common fee requirements: 1.48 requests require fee per 1.17(i); petitions to suspend action under 1.103(a) require fee per 1.17(g); petitions to withdraw application from issue under 1.313 require fee per 1.17(h); extensions under 1.136(a) require varying fees per 1.17(a)(1)-(5); requests to suspend under 1.103(b)/(c) require fee per 1.17(i); requests to defer examination under 1.103(d) require fee per 1.17(i) and publication fee per 1.18(d). Insert missing fee/item numbers and correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal dismissed — allowed claims but formal matters remaining (form paragraph 12.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of applicant’s failure to file a brief within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37(a), the appeal stands dismissed and the proceedings as to the rejected claims are considered terminated. This application will be passed to issue on allowed claim [1] provided the following formal matters are corrected. Prosecution is otherwise closed. Applicant is required to make the necessary corrections within a shortened statutory period set to expire TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this letter to avoid ABANDONMENT of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the notice of appeal was filed on or after January 23, 2012 and formal matters cannot be handled by examiner’s amendment (see MPEP § 1215.04). Insert description of formal matters to be corrected. Claims indicated as containing allowable subject matter but objected to as dependent upon a rejected claim are to be considered rejected (MPEP § 1215.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension to file appeal brief under 37 CFR 1.136(b) — granted (form paragraph 12.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(b) for filing the appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37 filed on [1] has been approved for [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For use if the notice of appeal was filed on or after January 23, 2012. Insert amount of time approved. This should be used only when 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not available or has been exhausted (e.g., litigation reissues or when appellant requests to reopen prosecution or file a reply brief as set forth in 37 CFR 41.39(b) and 41.50(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension to file appeal brief under 37 CFR 1.136(b) — denied (form paragraph 12.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(b) for filing the appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37 filed on [1] has been disapproved because no sufficient cause for the extension has been shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For use if the notice of appeal was filed on or after January 23, 2012. Use only when 37 CFR 1.136(a) is not available or has been exhausted. Insert date the request was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening of prosecution after appeal brief or amended appeal brief filed (form paragraph 12.239)
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the [1] filed on [2], PROSECUTION IS HEREBY REOPENED. [3] set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid abandonment, appellant must either (1) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (if the Office action is non-final) or a reply under 37 CFR 1.113 (if the Office action is final); or (2) initiate a new appeal by filing a notice of appeal under 37 CFR 41.31 followed by an appeal brief under 37 CFR 41.37. Previously paid notice of appeal fee and appeal brief fee can be applied to the new appeal; if fees increased since payment, appellant must pay the difference. A Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE) must approve reopening by signing.
